title: HerraduraKEx Protocol Specification
description: Machine-readable inventory of protocols, PEM wire-format labels, CLI --algo tags, security-level classification, and parameter sizes for the HerraduraKEx cryptographic suite. Generated by spec/generate_spec.py from the canonical source files listed in `generated_from` -- see spec/README.md. Consumers (tools or LLMs) should treat this file, not prose documentation, as the source of truth for exact wire-format strings and algo tags.

spec_version.description: Version of this spec document's structure (independent of the suite's own version).

generated_from.description: Source files this spec was mechanically generated from or cross-checked against.

wire_format_labels.description: PEM block labels (HerraduraCli/herradura_codec.h PEM_* constants) not already covered as a protocol's private/public key label -- session keys, signatures, ciphertexts, proofs, protocol-specific artifacts.

cli_subcommands.description: Every subcommand the CLI defines, keyed by name -- not only those taking --algo.

cross_implementation_gaps.description: Known feature-parity gaps between the C, Go, and Python CLIs (an algo tag or subcommand present in one but not another). Not exhaustive of every edge case -- see spec/README.md.

parameters.description: Protocol-family parameter sizes extracted from herradura.h / herradura/herradura.go constants (key bit widths, Stern-F/ZKP-NL/WOTS/HKEX-RNL round and dimension counts).

unfiled_cli_surface.description: CLI subcommands that reach no protocol entry (TODO #238 Part C). `pkey` is a utility; the rest are constructions that have never been security-classified, so filing them means classifying them. Enumerated here rather than left invisible; generate_spec.py fails on a NEW unaccounted-for subcommand.

cli_flag_matrix.description: Per-subcommand --flag support, derived from each CLI's OWN argument parser the way `cli_subcommands[*].algos` is derived from each CLI's own dispatch (TODO #267). Keyed by subcommand, then by flag, to a boolean per implementation. Keys are the UNION over all four CLIs, so a subcommand only one CLI defines (Go's `threshold-verify`) appears here even though `cli_subcommands` does not carry it. Flag GRANULARITY only: where a flag takes an enumerated value the value sets may still differ (`kex --kdf`), and that is recorded in `cli_surface_gaps[*].reason`, not derived.

cli_surface_gaps.description: Every non-unanimous cell of `cli_flag_matrix` and of the subcommand surface, joined to a curated reason (TODO #267). Derived, and exhaustive by construction: generate_spec.py refuses to emit a spec in which a gap has no recorded reason, or a recorded reason has no gap. `status` separates a deliberate per-language scope decision (`acknowledged`) from a real asymmetry that is merely recorded and counted (`defect`) -- TODO #267 closes on this mechanism, not on the ports, so `defect` rows are an expected steady state.

missing_from.description: For a flag gap, restricted to CLIs that define the subcommand at all -- `rand`'s flags are not also reported as missing from Java, which lacks `rand` itself.

cli_flag_value_gaps.description: The VALUE-set axis of the CLI surface, one granularity below `cli_surface_gaps` (TODO #269). That table answers whether a CLI defines a flag; this one answers which values it accepts, for the flags where the four disagree. Python's sets are DERIVED from argparse `choices=`; C, Go and Java accept values through chains of string comparisons and are curated in generate_spec.py's CLI_FLAG_VALUES, checked against the derived flag matrix in both directions. Exhaustive the same way every other table here is: an entry whose value sets have converged is an orphan and generation FAILS until it is deleted, so reaching value parity forces the row out rather than leaving a stale claim behind. `accepted_by_all` is the portable subset -- the values a caller may use against any of the four.

accepted_values.description: Per-language accepted value set, keyed by implementation.

accepted_by_all.description: Intersection: the values portable across every CLI that defines the flag.

divergent_values.description: Values at least one CLI accepts and at least one does not.

id.description: Stable protocol id. Equal to the --algo tag when the protocol has one; for protocols reached only through their own subcommands (aPAKE), an id with no tag behind it. See cli_binding.

pem_labels.description: PEM block labels this protocol's keys/artifacts use, when produced via genpkey/pkey.

cli_support.description: Which of the three CLI implementations accept this algo tag for at least one subcommand.

parameters.description: Protocol-specific parameter sizes (bit widths, round counts, etc). Keys vary by protocol family; see spec/README.md for the constant each key maps to.

status.description: production: suitable for its stated (classical or PQC) security claim at shipped parameters. demo-only: shipped parameters are intentionally below production soundness/security (see notes for the production parameter). pedagogical: exists to illustrate a construction, not to be used at all in a real deployment. deprecated: superseded, no further work planned. broken: a proof or exploit shows the construction fails its security goal. research: proposed/prototyped, not a shipped CLI algo.

quantum_resistant.description: true/false, or a string like "conjectured" when the claim is not proven.

cli_binding.description: How the CLI reaches this protocol: an --algo tag ('algo_flag', with the subcommands whose choices list carries it), its own subcommands ('subcommand', for protocols with no tag), a flag on an existing subcommand ('subcommand_flag', e.g. `fpe --v3`, which names the flag in 'flag'), or neither ('none').

flag.description: Only for kind 'subcommand_flag': the flag that selects this variant on the named subcommand.

algos.description: Maps each accepted --algo value to the list of CLI implementations that accept it for this subcommand.

protocol.description: For a subcommand with no --algo flag: the protocol id it implements, or null when it reaches none (see unfiled_cli_surface).

implementations.description: Which CLI implementations define this subcommand at all. TODO #267: `cli_subcommands` is keyed on the Python CLI's subparser list, so this is the only place a subcommand another CLI lacks (Java has no `rand`) becomes visible here.

cliSubcommand.description: Every CLI subcommand, keyed by name. Those with `has_algo_flag: true` carry an `algos` map; the rest name the protocol they implement, or record why they implement none.
